1_Periodo.titulo: 1.º Período: Family, Daily Routines & School Life
metas: Use Present Simple for daily habits and routines (3rd person singular -s/-es)
Use Present Continuous for actions happening at the moment of speaking
Apply Frequency Adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) in the correct word order

conceitos_chave.definicao: Used for routines, habits and facts. Key words: every day, always, usually, on Mondays. Rule: He/She/It + verb-s/es.
Used for actions happening now. Rule: am/is/are + verb-ing. Key words: now, at the moment, right now, Look!, Listen!.
Placed BEFORE main verbs (ex: 'He often plays football'), but AFTER the verb to be (ex: 'She is always on time').

topicos.imagem_legenda: Grammar box comparing Present Simple (routine) with Present Continuous (action in progress).

foco_teste.questao_exemplo: Complete the sentences with Present Simple or Present Continuous: (a) Listen! Mark ______ (play) the guitar in his room. (b) My parents usually ______ (go) to work by train.
foco_teste.proposta_resolucao: (a) is playing (action happening right now indicated by 'Listen!'). (b) go (routine action indicated by the frequency adverb 'usually').
foco_teste.criterio_cotacao: Correct verb form for each sentence (50% each).
foco_teste.erro_frequente: Forgetting the auxiliary 'is/are' in the continuous tense or adding '-s' to verbs with 'I/You/We/They'.

flashcards.frente: Where do adverbs of frequency go in a sentence with the verb TO BE?
flashcards.verso: They go AFTER the verb to be (ex: 'She is never late').

flashcards.frente: When do you use Present Continuous?
flashcards.verso: For actions happening at the exact moment of speaking (now, at the moment, Look!).

metas: Describe rooms, furniture and prepositions of place (next to, behind, opposite, between)
Use Comparative of Superiority (short adjectives -er than; long adjectives more ... than)
Use Superlative of Superiority (the -est / the most ...)

conceitos_chave.definicao: Adj + -er + than (ex: tall ➔ taller than; big ➔ bigger than; easy ➔ easier than).
more + Adj + than (ex: comfortable ➔ more comfortable than; expensive ➔ more expensive than).
good ➔ better ➔ the best; bad ➔ worse ➔ the worst; far ➔ further ➔ the furthest.

topicos.imagem_legenda: Summary chart showing short, long, and irregular comparative and superlative forms.

foco_teste.questao_exemplo: Complete with the correct comparative or superlative form: (a) London is ________ (busy) than Porto. (b) This sofa is ________________ (comfortable) in the whole house.
foco_teste.proposta_resolucao: (a) busier (short adjective ending in -y: changes to -ier + than). (b) the most comfortable (long adjective in superlative context: the most + adjective).
foco_teste.criterio_cotacao: Correct spelling and comparative/superlative structure (50% each).
foco_teste.erro_frequente: Writing 'more busier' (double comparative) or forgetting 'the' before superlatives.

flashcards.frente: What are the comparative and superlative forms of 'good' and 'bad'?
flashcards.verso: Good ➔ better than ➔ the best. Bad ➔ worse than ➔ the worst.

flashcards.frente: How do you form the comparative of a long adjective like 'modern'?
flashcards.verso: more modern than (never add -er to long adjectives).

3_Periodo.titulo: 3.º Período: Past Experiences, Free Time & Sports
metas: Use Past Simple with regular verbs (-ed) and irregular verbs (went, saw, bought, had)
Form negative and interrogative sentences in Past Simple with 'did / didn't'
Distinguish countable and uncountable nouns (some, any, much, many, a lot of)

conceitos_chave.definicao: Add -ed to base form: play ➔ played, live ➔ lived, study ➔ studied, stop ➔ stopped (CVC rule).
Memorized 2nd column list: go ➔ went, have ➔ had, see ➔ saw, buy ➔ bought, write ➔ wrote, eat ➔ ate.
Auxiliary DID: Did you visit London? / I didn't visit London. The main verb stays in the INFINITIVE!

topicos.imagem_legenda: Past Simple affirmative, negative (didn't + inf) and question (Did + subj + inf) structures.

foco_teste.questao_exemplo: Turn the sentence into negative and question: 'Sarah went to the sports club yesterday.'
foco_teste.proposta_resolucao: Negative: Sarah didn't go to the sports club yesterday. Question: Did Sarah go to the sports club yesterday?
foco_teste.criterio_cotacao: Use of didn't / Did (50%) and returning 'went' to base form 'go' (50%).
foco_teste.erro_frequente: Writing 'didn't went' (wrong! Auxiliary already carries the past, verb must be in base form).

flashcards.frente: What is the past simple of 'buy', 'see', and 'go'?
flashcards.verso: Buy ➔ bought; See ➔ saw; Go ➔ went.

flashcards.frente: Is 'I didn't saw the film' correct?
flashcards.verso: No! Correct is: 'I didn't see the film' (after didn't, the verb is always in the bare infinitive).
